notes: Outside ROOM_HOUSE, C returns the exact must-be-in-your-house line before control lookup or argument parsing.
The shared POS_RESTING dispatcher rejection is owned by the existing fade position-gate vehicle.
A bare house command emits the two-line C usage text.
An owner with no guests receives the exact header and None line.
An unknown guest name reaches the exact No such player branch.
C-first guest client Houseguest is in the controlled house while Testor owns it; house guest Houseguest reaches the primary-owner refusal before guest lookup (R1/R2/R5e/R5h).
The online guest is added and C's success byte matches.
The post-add listing returns the title-cased online guest name.
Repeating the guest name toggles the record entry out and emits Guest deleted.
C two_arguments skips the fill word before Guest and discards trailing words; the focused test pins the resulting add.
A transfer without a target emits the exact C prompt.
An unknown transfer target emits No such player.
A valid target changes the in-memory owner and preserves C's intentional transfered spelling.

An independent level-38 observer with normal syslog receives the exact C transfer audit line when Testor transfers the house to Houseguest; the actor's "House transfered." confirmation is separately checked (R1/R2/R5e/R5h).
After Testor transfers the house to Houseguest, the former owner issues house guest Houseguest and receives C's exact primary-owner refusal (R1/R2/R5e/R5h).
An unrecognized first token falls through the handler silently; Go no longer invents a usage fallback.

C sets ROOM_HOUSE only while loading an accepted house-control record or after creating that record; hcontrol destroy clears both. The shipped world has no static ROOM_HOUSE bits, so a flagged room without a record requires corrupted/out-of-game state; the Go unit injects that invalid topology (R1/R2/R4/R5e/R5g).
Missing guest IDs are removed from the list before the visible guest listing and control save.

C-first owner adds a distinct online candidate against a valid control record already holding all 50 guest IDs; the candidate reaches MAX_GUESTS and receives the exact refusal before mutation (R1/R2/R5e/R5h).

C resolves the existing offline Oraklet record through the persistent player index; Go now does the same through the DB-backed pair in pkg/session/manager.go (pkg/db/house_lookup.go:13-26) and adds the guest (R1/R2/R5e/R5g/R5h).

C resolves offline guest ID 2 to Oraklet through the persistent player index; Go resolves it the same way and lists Oraklet (pkg/session/manager.go; pkg/game/house_player.go:99-137) (R1/R2/R5e/R5g/R5h).
C transfers the house to offline Oraklet by persistent id; Go resolves the id through the DB pair and transfers (pkg/session/manager.go; pkg/game/house_player.go:140-165) (R1/R2/R5e/R5g/R5h).
The successful transfer updates the control owner without changing unrelated guest state.
C do_house does not call House_save_control after transfer; the focused test pins the existing file owner.
No-DB runtime players receive distinct IDs after the first zero-ID player so the C-style guest ID/name lookup cannot alias the owner.

C never writes house contents: every House_crashsave caller is commented out and House_save_all is a stub, so a player-dropped object in a house is per-boot state. The scenario drops a loaf in the house at 8162, proves it lying there, then <RESTART>s and proves the room empty on both engines — the port reproduces the non-persistence rather than improving it (R4).

L1 house.c:182,189: both sprintf arms feed perror() -- "SYSERR: Error deleting house file #%d. (1)/(2)" -- and run only when unlink/open fail, i.e. filesystem-error paths outside any player output (R4/R5e).
